declared.title: Higher income is associated with greater life satisfaction, and more stress
declared.foundIn: Europe PMC search « (income OR money) AND ("emotional well-being" OR "experienced well-being" OR "life evaluation") AND (satiation OR plateau OR threshold) » (2026-11-22)

population: 2.05 million US adults, Gallup Daily Poll 2008-2017

findings.text: Above about $63,000 of household income, people are more likely to report stress the day before

support.sentence: Drawing upon responses from 2.05 million U.S. adults from the Gallup Daily Poll from 2008 to 2017 we find that with household income above ~$63,000 respondents are more likely to experience stress.

limits: cross-sectional: an association, not an effect of money
stress is a yes/no question about the previous day, the measure family of Kahneman & Deaton 2010
the title's « greater life satisfaction » is not stated as a result sentence in the abstract: not used here
